title: Floating-point conversion leak as a learning curve: signatures-to-key vs channel noise and tree level, simulated oracle, n=16..128
claim: KN-LIT-7909ee reports Falcon key recovery from tens of power traces that leak the signed exponent of each ffSampling center at integer-to-float conversion. Abstract that leak as a noisy channel (exponent bucket of each center, flipped to a neighbouring bucket with probability eps) on a self-built toy Falcon. The claim: the median number of signatures to certified key recovery N*(n, eps) scales as C * n^b / I(eps), with I(eps) the per-center mutual information of the channel, b in [0, 1.5], and leaks restricted to the top half of the tree carry at least twice the key information per leaked bit of leaf-only leaks. Falsified if N* is not monotone in I(eps) or the log-log fit in n leaves residuals above 0.3 in log2 N*.
mechanism: Each center c_i is an affine function of the target and of previously drawn integers through the secret ffLDL tree, so an exponent bucket is a two-sided interval constraint on a secret-dependent linear form. Many signatures give many intervals; maximum-likelihood over the bucket observations turns them into approximate linear hints, and lattice reduction finishes the key, which is the reported pipeline. The information per observation is bounded by the bucket entropy times the channel capacity, so signature count should track 1/I(eps). Top-level centers are larger dense combinations of more secret coordinates, so a bit there should constrain more of the key than a leaf bit.
tracked_object: N*(n, eps, level): median over 10 self-generated keys of the number of simulated-leak signatures needed until the recovered (f, g) satisfies h = g/f mod q and reproduces a verifying signature.

predictions.falsified_by: ratio below 1.3 at n = 64 with 10 keys
ratio at or below 1 at both n

predictions.metric: log-log slope b of N* in n at eps = 0
predictions.falsified_by: b outside [0, 1.5] or residual > 0.3 log2 units

minimal_test.design: Python port of a toy Falcon (q = 12289, n in {16, 32, 64, 128}) with an exponent-leak oracle wrapped around ffSampling; attacker: bucket MLE then BKZ (fpylll) on the hint-embedded lattice; sweep eps and leaked level.

positive: eps = 0 and full-precision center values leaked; recovery must succeed within a handful of signatures
A/A: identical configuration run on two disjoint key/seed blocks; N* ratio sets the noise floor

falsification_conditions: N* not monotone in I(eps) across the 4 noise levels at n = 64
null-oracle arm recovers the key in any trial (pipeline leaks the key by another path)
positive control fails, so the attack harness is not able to see a leak
confounders: BKZ block size cap limits recovery independently of hint count
the toy port's tree depth differs from the reference implementation at small n
MLE initialization quality dominating the hint information
interpretation_limits: Scale and transfer: toy n up to 128 with a simulated channel; transfer to n = 512/1024 assumes the fitted n^b law holds and is not a statement about any physical device or deployed implementation
The channel model is an abstraction of KN-LIT-7909ee, whose own counts were not reproduced here

title: Float-free integer Gram-root sampler vs ffSampling: is the integer sampler's covariance error aligned with the secret basis?
claim: The float-free perturbation sampler (KN-LIT-4528, built on Peikert's perturbation approach, KN-LIT-2472) replaces a real square root of a key-dependent covariance by an integral approximation. Its output covariance error E = Cov(s) - sigma^2 I is therefore a function of the key Gram matrix. Claim: E's mass concentrates on the subspace spanned by the shortest secret rotations with an alignment z-score >= 3 against random subspaces of equal dimension, while float64 ffSampling at the same n has z < 2. Falsified if the integer sampler's alignment is within noise of random subspaces.
mechanism: The perturbation covariance is s^2 I minus a multiple of B^T B, so the matrix whose integral root is approximated carries the secret Gram explicitly. Approximation residuals of a matrix root are concentrated along that matrix's eigenvectors, which here are built from secret directions. ffSampling's rounding errors enter through many tree nodes and largely average into an isotropic-looking error. So the two float-free versus float designs can differ in leak geometry even at equal total divergence.
tracked_object: Alignment score a = ||P_K E P_K||_F / ||E||_F with P_K the projector onto span of the n rotations of (g, -f), reported as a z-score against 1000 random n-dimensional subspaces.

predictions.metric: alignment z difference integer minus ffSampling

minimal_test.design: Compute E analytically from each sampler's exact construction where possible and confirm empirically with 10^6 signatures per key at n in {16, 32, 64}.
controls: null: exact-rational root sampler (E = 0 up to sampling noise) and random subspaces
positive: planted E = eps * B^T B with known eps
A/A: same arm on two disjoint key-seed blocks

falsification_conditions: integer-root alignment z < 2 at n = 32 and 64
positive control not detected at eps = 1e-3
confounders: the toy integer-root construction differing from the published one
basis choice for P_K when rotations are not orthogonal
interpretation_limits: Scale and transfer: n <= 64 toy keys; transfer assumes the root-approximation residual structure is dimension-independent
Alignment is a geometry statement, not a recovery; the signatures-to-key cost is not measured here

heuristic_assumptions.statement: Root approximation residuals align with the dominant eigenvectors of the target matrix
heuristic_assumptions.rigorous_support: standard perturbation theory for matrix functions
heuristic_assumptions.validation_plan: check residual-eigenvector overlap directly on the computed roots

target_complexity.time_exponent: O(n^3) per key for exact covariance
target_complexity.best_known: no published measurement of leak geometry for float-free samplers (as far as recalled)
target_complexity.tradeoff_note: measurement of a structural property; constant-level, defensive

title: Weakest-key census at n=512/1024: how close does the smallest ffLDL leaf width of accepted keys come to the base sampler floor?
claim: Sampler deviation depends on per-key leaf widths sigma_i = sigma / ||b~_i||, and analyses quote the worst case allowed by keygen acceptance. Key generation is cheap, so the per-key distribution of the minimum leaf width can be measured at deployed dimension on self-generated keys. Claim: the minimum leaf width over accepted keys has a lower tail reaching within 1% of the base sampler's declared floor sigma_min (RECALLED about 1.2778 for n = 512) for at least 1 key in 10^4, and the argmin falls in the last eighth of the tree order in at least 80% of keys. Falsified if no key in 10^5 comes within 3% of the floor, or the argmin is spread uniformly.
mechanism: Leaf widths are sigma over Gram-Schmidt norms of the secret basis in ffLDL order. Keygen accepts on norm bounds that limit, but do not pin, the largest Gram-Schmidt norm. Gram-Schmidt norms decay along the basis, so the largest b~_i (smallest leaf width) sits at a predictable position. Base-sampler approximation error grows as width approaches its floor, so the keys near the floor are the ones where any arithmetic defect is largest: risk is a tail property of the key population, not an average.
tracked_object: Per-key m = min_i sigma_i / sigma_min and argmin position, over accepted keys.

predictions.metric: fraction of argmin in last eighth of tree order

minimal_test.design: Run reference keygen 10^5 times per n with logged tree constants; compute m and argmin; compare with an idealised keygen without rejection and with planted degraded keys.
controls: null: keygen without the acceptance rejection (shows what rejection removes)
positive: keys with (F, G) left unreduced by adding k(f, g), which must show m near or below 1
A/A: two disjoint seed blocks of 5x10^4 keys

falsification_conditions: no key within 3% of floor in 10^5 at n = 512
confounders: the declared sigma_min value is recalled, not read from the standard
different reference implementations computing tree constants differently (see F4)
interpretation_limits: Scale and transfer: runs at deployed n but measures only key-population tree constants of self-generated keys; it says nothing about leakage of any fielded key
A low margin is not a measured divergence; that needs a leaf-level divergence model

heuristic_assumptions.rigorous_support: plausible from the Bernoulli-exponential and table construction; not proven here
heuristic_assumptions.validation_plan: compute exact leaf output divergence at 10 widths across the range

title: Tower NTRUSolve vs exact rational Babai on the same (f,g): does approximate field-norm reduction leave slack in (F,G)?
claim: NTRUSolve (KN-LIT-4954) lifts a solution of fG - gF = q up the power-of-two tower via the field norm and size-reduces (F, G) against (f, g) at every level with approximate arithmetic. Two correct solvers can return (F, G) differing by k(f, g). Claim: on identical (f, g) at n = 512, the tower solver and an exact-rational Babai reduction disagree on (F, G) for at least 1% of keys; when they disagree, the largest Gram-Schmidt norm of the full basis differs by at least 0.5%, and at least 1 key in 10^3 is accepted by one solver and rejected by the other. Falsified if outputs are identical on 10^4 keys.
mechanism: Size reduction computes k = round((F f* + G g*)/(f f* + g g*)) in approximate precision; near-half fractional parts round differently under truncated precision, and errors at a lower tower level propagate through the lift. The final basis quality sets leaf widths, so solver choice changes the per-key leaf margins of F3 and the acceptance set of keygen without changing correctness.
tracked_object: Per-key indicator of (F, G) disagreement and Delta = log max_i ||b~_i|| (tower) minus log max_i ||b~_i|| (exact).

minimal_test.design: Run both solvers on the same 10^4 (f, g) per n; compare outputs and basis quality.
controls: null: same solver run twice (A/A) must agree bitwise
positive: tower solver with reduction skipped at one level must show large Delta
A/A: tower solver on two seed blocks for the population statistics

confounders: exact solver choosing a different but equally reduced representative
interpretation_limits: Scale and transfer: run at n = 64..1024 on self-generated keys; implications for leakage pass through F3's margin model and are not measured here
Slack in (F, G) is not itself a leak

title: Same fixed-KL planted defect in ffSampling, Mitaka and Antrag-keyed Mitaka: how many signatures until the basis leaks?
claim: Mitaka (KN-LIT-4936) replaces Falcon's ffSampling by a hybrid sampler and Antrag (KN-LIT-2565) changes keygen to make Mitaka's quality close to Falcon's. Plant the same defect family (one-leaf width miscalibration) scaled to an identical per-signature KL divergence delta in each. Claim: the number of signatures for a second-moment learner to estimate a secret direction to angle < 10 degrees differs between ffSampling and Mitaka by at least 2x at n = 32 and 64, and Antrag keys move Mitaka at least halfway toward ffSampling. Falsified if all three are within 1.5x at every delta.
mechanism: Equal KL does not mean equal information about the basis: the defect enters the output law through the sampler's own decomposition (ffLDL tree vs per-embedding hybrid sampling), which rotates where the defect lands relative to secret directions. A learner reads only the key-dependent part, so the Fisher information about the basis per signature can differ at matched KL.
tracked_object: N_theta: signatures until the learned top eigenvector of the residual covariance lies within 10 degrees of a true secret rotation, per sampler and delta.

predictions.metric: fraction of gap closed by Antrag keys

minimal_test.design: Toy implementations of the three samplers at n in {16, 32, 64}; planted width miscalibration tuned to delta in {1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1} by exact KL computation; second-moment learner on residuals.
controls: null: delta = 0 in each sampler (learner angle must stay at the random-direction distribution)
positive: delta = 0.3
A/A: same sampler on two key-seed blocks

falsification_conditions: ratio within [0.67, 1.5] for all delta at n = 32 and 64
confounders: different sigma per sampler changes baseline variance
interpretation_limits: Scale and transfer: toy n <= 64 and a planted defect family; deployed samplers' real defects are not measured
learner is second-moment only; higher-order learners may reorder samplers

title: Are FN-DSA's norm-bound and fixed-length-encoding restarts key-independent, and do they select on a defective sampler's leak?
claim: Signing restarts when ||(s1, s2)||^2 exceeds the bound or (RECALLED, padded format) when compressed s2 overflows its fixed slot. Under the ideal law both events are functions of a key-independent distribution, so accepted signatures stay key-independent. Claim A: with an exact sampler, per-key restart rates over 200 keys are homogeneous (chi-square p > 0.01). Claim B: under a planted defect whose width error depends on the key, the restart rate becomes key-dependent (p < 1e-3) and the accepted law's divergence from ideal differs from the unconditioned law's by a factor kappa with |log kappa| >= 0.1. Distinct from the encoding-nullspace audit: the object is the selection induced by restarts.
mechanism: Rejection on a public function conditions the output law. If the pre-rejection law is key-independent, conditioning cannot create key dependence. If it is defective in a key-dependent way, rejection reweights the defect: tail-heavy defects are partly removed (kappa < 1), others can be concentrated. Restart counts are an extra observable for anyone timing signing, so key-dependent rates are a leak independent of signature values.
tracked_object: Per-key restart rate r_k and kappa = KL(accepted || ideal accepted) / KL(pre-rejection || ideal).

predictions.metric: homogeneity p-value of r_k, exact sampler

title: Subfield-trace projections of signatures as public detectors: does power peak at the degree matching a defect's tree level?
claim: In Z[x]/(x^n + 1) the relative trace to the index-2 subfield returns twice the even part, the same split ffSampling recurses on. Claim: for a defect planted at ffLDL tree depth l, a quadratic statistic on the public relative trace of (s1, s2) to degree n/2^l reaches 80% power with at least 2x fewer signatures than the same statistic on the full 2n-dimensional signature, at n = 64 and l in {3, 5}. Falsified if the full-dimensional statistic is never worse than the best trace statistic.
mechanism: A deep-level defect perturbs a low-dimensional component; a statistic over all 2n coordinates pays noise in every dimension. If the trace maps keep most of the defect while discarding dimensions, power per signature rises. Because the secret basis has entries in the top field, the trace does not commute with the secret frame, so whether the defect survives the projection is exactly what is tested.
tracked_object: Signatures to 80% power at alpha = 0.01 for each statistic family and defect level.

predictions.minimum_effect: equals n/2^l within one tower step

minimal_test.design: Toy ffSampling at n = 64 with planted center bias at depth l; compute statistics for trace degrees 1..64; 500 replicate experiments per cell for power.
controls: null: exact sampler, all statistics
positive: planted defect at top level (l = 0)
A/A: exact sampler on two seed blocks to calibrate false-positive rate

falsification_conditions: full statistic as good or better at every l
confounders: statistic dimension changing the null distribution shape
interpretation_limits: Scale and transfer: n = 64 toy with planted defects; transfer assumes tower structure scales unchanged to 512/1024
Power on planted defects says nothing about whether the real sampler has a defect

heuristic_assumptions.statement: Planted center bias at depth l is representative of real deep-level defects

title: Score the LWE-with-hints estimator on center-exponent hints: predicted vs measured BKZ block size at n=32..128
claim: Extrapolating any leak-to-key curve to n = 512/1024 will go through a hint-integration estimator (recalled: Dachman-Soled, Ducas, Gong, Rossi framework). Center-exponent buckets map to approximate hints with variance set by bucket width. Claim: the estimator's predicted block size is within +-5 of the measured minimal successful block size at n = 64 and 128 for 20 to 200 signatures of hints; if errors exceed 10 or are one-sided across n, the estimator cannot carry the curve to deployed n.
mechanism: The framework updates the lattice volume and the secret's covariance ellipsoid with each hint and predicts block size from a GSA-style model. Bucket hints are interval constraints, not Gaussian, and they are correlated within a signature; both break the framework's assumptions in measurable ways that scale with the hint count.

title: Maximum-likelihood trapdoor recovery from a defective sampler vs moment learners and the Cramer-Rao bound
claim: Detection is not recovery. For a planted defect of known functional form, the signature likelihood given the basis is computable up to normalisation at toy n. Claim: a gradient-based MLE over basis parameters recovers a secret direction to 10 degrees with at most one third of the signatures needed by second- and fourth-moment learners (the NTRUSign-attack family) at n in {8, 16, 32}, and reaches within 2x of the Cramer-Rao bound. Falsified if MLE needs at least as many signatures as the best moment method at any n.
mechanism: Moment learners use only a few low-order statistics, which carry a fraction of the Fisher information when the defect is non-Gaussian (centre bias, truncation). MLE uses the full law. The surrogate is a smooth relaxation of the discrete Gaussian with planted defect, differentiable in the basis; Riemannian ascent on the orthogonal-like parameterisation avoids symmetry traps by multiple restarts.
tracked_object: N_theta for MLE and moment learners, and the ratio to the numerically computed Cramer-Rao lower bound.

MLE converges to the true basis under the null

interpretation_limits: Scale and transfer: n <= 32 and a known defect form; at deployed n the likelihood is intractable without this structure

title: Annular (Antrag) keys flatten the embedding spectrum: are they farther from the dense-sublattice regime than Falcon keys?
claim: Antrag (KN-LIT-2565) samples (f, g) so that |f(z)|^2 + |g(z)|^2 lies in an annulus at every embedding z. Gram of the rotation orbit in canonical coordinates is diagonal with those values, so by AM-GM a flat spectrum maximises the orbit covolume at a given norm: the dense sublattice is less dense. Claim: at n in {32, 64} and matched ||(f, g)||, the dense-sublattice transition modulus q* for Antrag-style keys is higher than for Falcon-accepted keys by at least 0.1 in log2 q, and keys with planted skewed spectra sit lower. Falsified if the shift is within the A/A noise.
mechanism: Covolume of the rank-n orbit equals the product of sqrt(|f(z)|^2 + |g(z)|^2) over embeddings, up to a ring constant. Fixed sum (norm), product maximal when values equal. The fatigue event is driven by orbit density relative to q^n, so flattening the spectrum pushes the event to larger q, and conversely Falcon's rejection only on norms leaves spectral spread.
tracked_object: log2 q* (50% DSD-event point by profile detection plus certified recovery) per key family at matched norm.

minimal_test.design: Three key families at n = 32, 64 with norms matched by rescaling; sweep q on a log grid; BKZ to beta = 30; detect event and certify recovery.
controls: null: Gaussian keys conditioned on norm only
positive: planted skewed-spectrum keys
A/A: Falcon family on two seed blocks

falsification_conditions: no shift between Antrag and Falcon families beyond noise
confounders: matching norm vs matching coefficient distribution
interpretation_limits: Scale and transfer: n <= 64; FN-DSA q = 12289 is far below fatigue at n = 512, so this is a direction-of-effect claim
Not a security statement for Antrag or FN-DSA

title: One randomness tape, three conforming builds: signature disagreement rates for emulated, strict and FMA-contracted FN-DSA
claim: Reference Falcon code (RECALLED) ships an integer-emulated floating-point backend and a native one, and compilers may contract a*b + c into FMA, changing rounding. Claim: on self-generated keys and identical RNG tapes, emulated and strict-native builds produce bit-identical signatures on 10^6 signatures, while FMA-contracted builds disagree on a fraction >= 1e-5 of signatures at n = 512. Each disagreement is a real-world arithmetic defect instance at deployed dimension; its first-differing tree node locates it.
mechanism: IEEE-754 binary64 with correct rounding is deterministic, so a faithful emulation matches strict native. FMA rounds once instead of twice, so it changes some centres by one ulp; a one-ulp centre change flips the sampled integer only when the centre sits near a decision boundary, which happens at a rate set by width and precision. The flip rate measured here is the empirical counterpart of the p-bit flip-set model.
tracked_object: Disagreement rate per build pair and the histogram of first-differing tree nodes.

positive: one operation forced to float32 must disagree often
A/A: strict vs strict across two run orders

falsification_conditions: emulated vs strict disagree (emulation not faithful)
confounders: library math functions not covered by emulation
interpretation_limits: Scale and transfer: deployed n on self-generated keys; disagreement does not imply leakage; no fielded device or key is involved

title: A shared positive-control ladder: five planted sampler defect types at exact KL, and each detector's minimum detectable KL
claim: Each detector in this lane brings its own positive control, so sensitivities cannot be compared. Build a shared ladder at n in {8, 16}: five defect types (leaf width scale, centre bias, tail truncation, sibling copula, p-bit rounding) at six exactly computed KL levels. Claim: for a fixed generic quadratic detector, the minimum detectable KL at 10^5 signatures differs by at least 10x between defect types, so a single power number per detector is meaningless; the ladder yields a detector-by-defect sensitivity matrix. Falsified if minimum detectable KL is within 3x across types.
mechanism: KL is an average; detectors see the defect through particular statistics, and defect types put their divergence in different places (tails, means, dependence). Exact KL at n <= 16 is computable by support enumeration, so rungs are known without sampling error.

title: Measured hybrid MITM vs primal BKZ on NTRU Prime-shaped rings, p=61..113: does the hybrid gain vanish past the transition?
claim: On Z[x]/(x^p - x - 1) with fixed-weight ternary secrets and q below the fatigue point, Howgrave-Graham's hybrid (KN-LIT-2084) with a measured optimal guess dimension r beats plain primal BKZ in total measured work by at least 2x for p >= 89, and r grows linearly in p. Once q passes the measured dense-sublattice transition, the hybrid advantage falls to at most 1.2x. So distance from fatigue and hybrid distance are different coordinates and must both be reported.
mechanism: Below fatigue the lattice behaves like LWE; guessing a sparse ternary tail via MITM removes dimensions at a combinatorial cost lower than BKZ's for those dimensions. Above fatigue the dense sublattice makes BKZ succeed at small block size, so the reduction half becomes cheap and guessing no longer pays.
tracked_object: Measured total work (BKZ node count plus MITM table operations, converted to CPU-seconds on one pinned core) at optimal r, versus primal BKZ alone, per (p, q).

minimal_test.design: p in {61, 73, 89, 101, 113}; weight w scaled as in the deployed ratio (RECALLED w/p about 0.38); q at three levels relative to measured transition; r swept.
controls: null: matched random lattice of same dimension and determinant with no planted secret (both attacks must fail)
positive: very low weight secrets where the hybrid must win
A/A: primal arm on two seed blocks

falsification_conditions: hybrid never beats primal by 2x below transition
interpretation_limits: Scale and transfer: p <= 113; sntrup761 is far larger, so only slopes are transferred with stated CI

title: Scaling-collapse test for matrix NTRU: is the transition a function of flattened dimension and dense-sublattice rank ratio only?
claim: For matrix NTRU with invertible secret F (d x d over R) and G (m x d), the lattice has dimension (d + m)n and a dense sublattice of rank dn, ratio rho = d/(d + m). Claim: log2 q* collapses onto a single function of N = (d + m)n and rho across (d, m) in {(1,1), (1,2), (2,1), (2,2), (1,3)}, with residuals below 0.15 in log2 q; the ring rank-1 case sits on the curve. Distinct from IDEA-20260809-2866e0, which locates the transition per rank: here a specific collapse law is tested and the rectangular lever varies rho independently of N.
mechanism: The dense-sublattice event depends on the sublattice's rank and covolume relative to the full lattice's determinant and dimension. If ring or module structure only enters through those, all variants with equal (N, rho) and secret norm behave alike. A failure of collapse would indicate structure beyond geometry, e.g., module automorphisms.
tracked_object: log2 q* per (d, m, n) with bootstrap CI and residual from the fitted collapse function.

title: Symplectic BKZ vs plain BKZ on NTRU lattices of dimension 128..220: measured speedup and dense-sublattice event location
claim: NTRU lattices are proportional to symplectic lattices (KN-LIT-6918), and reduction that preserves the symplectic form only needs to reduce half the basis, recalled as about a 2x LLL speedup. Claim: a symplectic BKZ variant gives a measured work speedup in [1.5, 2.5]x for full BKZ-beta tours at dimension 128..220, and the block size at which the dense-sublattice event triggers is unchanged within +-2. Falsified if speedup < 1.2 or > 4, or if the event block size shifts by more than 4.
mechanism: The symplectic form pairs basis vector i with 2n+1-i; reducing the first half determines the second via the dual. BKZ on the full basis does redundant work. The profile of a symplectic reduced basis is anti-symmetric around its midpoint, which may change how the dense-sublattice's projection appears in the middle of the profile.

title: NTRU Prime's unbalanced secret (3f,g): how the dense-sublattice transition moves with block-norm ratio, with and without rescaling
claim: In Streamlined NTRU Prime (RECALLED) h = g/(3f), so the short vector in the NTRU lattice is (3f, g) with block norms differing by a ratio r (about 3 sqrt(w) / sqrt(2p/3), RECALLED shapes). The fatigue law assumes balanced blocks. Claim: without rescaling, log2 q* shifts by at least 0.5 log2 r relative to balanced; with the optimal diagonal rescaling of one block, the shift is at most 0.1 log2 r. So the deployed distance must be quoted after rescaling. Falsified if the unrescaled shift is absent.
mechanism: Lattice reduction sees Euclidean norms; an unbalanced secret is longer than necessary in one block and the dense orbit's covolume rises. Scaling the first block by 1/r (a standard primal-attack trick) restores balance and the dense-sublattice event should return to the balanced location.
tracked_object: log2 q* versus r, rescaled and unrescaled.

minimal_test.design: Ring x^p - x - 1 and x^n + 1 at dims 2n in {122, 146, 178}; secrets (c f, g) with c in {1, 2, 3, 5}; rescale arm.
controls: null: matched random lattice
positive: c = 1 balanced
A/A: c = 3 on two seed blocks

confounders: rounding the scale factor to integers
interpretation_limits: Scale and transfer: toy dimension; deployed distance correction transferred as a shift in log2 q with CI
no claim about sntrup761 safety

heuristic_assumptions.statement: Optimal rescaling is the norm-ratio factor
heuristic_assumptions.validation_plan: sweep scale factor and find empirical optimum

title: Is the measured fatigue point a lattice property or a reducer property? BKZ 2.0 vs G6K vs progressive sieve at matched work
claim: This goal will report a measured q*. Claim: the location log2 q* measured with three reducers at matched work budget differs by less than its CI width (target < 0.1 log2 q); if it differs more, the fatigue point must be reported per reducer. Distinct from IDEA-20260809-2976d8, which scores an estimator: this compares reducers on identical instances.
mechanism: The event is defined by the reduction reaching the dense sublattice; different reducers at equal cost reach different profile shapes (sieving has dimensions for free, BKZ 2.0 uses pruned enumeration). If the event depends on profile shape near the middle, location may move with reducer.
tracked_object: log2 q* per reducer at equal CPU-second budget on identical instances.

title: Does hybrid guessing destroy the dense sublattice? Projected NTRU residuals vs matched random uSVP after fixing k coefficients
claim: Hybrid attacks guess k coordinates and reduce a projected lattice of dimension 2n - k. Claim: the residual retains a dense sublattice of rank about n - k, so its transition q*(k) falls as k grows; at k = n/8, log2 q* drops by at least 5% relative to k = 0. If instead the residual is indistinguishable from a matched random uSVP instance (event signature absent), guessing destroys the dense sublattice and hybrid and fatigue attacks cannot be combined.
mechanism: Rotations x^i (f, g) that avoid guessed coordinates survive projection intact; others are perturbed by known amounts. The surviving orbit is a dense sublattice in fewer dimensions with the same q, which is relatively more overstretched. Whether enough rotations survive depends on which coordinates are guessed (contiguous windows preserve more).
tracked_object: log2 q*(k) in the projected lattice and profile event signature against matched random uSVP.

predictions.metric: relative drop of log2 q* at k = n/8

predictions.minimum_effect: present in >= 80% at q above q*(k)

minimal_test.design: n in {48, 64, 80} on x^n + 1 with correct guesses (oracle) of k in {0, n/16, n/8, n/4}, contiguous vs scattered positions.
controls: null: random uSVP of same dimension and gap
positive: unprojected overstretched NTRU
A/A: k = 0 on two seed blocks

falsification_conditions: no drop in q* with k
confounders: oracle guesses hide MITM cost (deliberate here)
interpretation_limits: Scale and transfer: n <= 80 with oracle guesses; the full hybrid cost is not measured here
no deployed claim

heuristic_assumptions.statement: Surviving rotation count controls residual density
heuristic_assumptions.validation_plan: count surviving rotations and regress q*

title: Rotations in x^p-x-1 are not isometries: norm growth, orbit covolume excess, and predicted vs measured transition shift
claim: Multiplication by x in Z[x]/(x^p - x - 1) sends the top coefficient to two positions, so ||x^i f|| grows with i instead of staying constant as in x^n + 1. Claim: the rotation orbit's covolume exceeds the anticyclic orbit's at matched secret norm by a measurable factor, a best-window choice of k consecutive rotations gives the densest rank-k sublattice, and the predicted transition shift from covolume ratio matches the measured shift within 50% with correct sign. Distinct from IDEA-20260809-263751 (black-box comparison) and IDEA-20260816-6e6f2e (correlation factor with constant diagonal), which assume or ignore the diagonal: here the diagonal itself is the mechanism.
mechanism: Each wrap adds a coefficient, so norms grow roughly as sqrt(1 + i/p)-type factors over a full orbit (to be measured). Larger diagonal in the Gram matrix means larger covolume, a less dense sublattice and a higher q*. The densest sublattice may be a window of low-growth rotations of rank below p.
tracked_object: Orbit log-covolume ratio NTRU-Prime/anticyclic, best-window rank, predicted and measured Delta log2 q*.

minimal_test.design: p in {61, 73, 89, 101} vs nearest power-of-two-like anticyclic dims; exact covolume computation; transition sweep.
controls: null: matched random lattice
positive: anticyclic ring (no growth)
A/A: x^p - x - 1 on two seed blocks

falsification_conditions: measured shift opposite in sign to prediction
confounders: dimension mismatch between prime p and anticyclic n
interpretation_limits: Scale and transfer: p <= 101; transfer to 761 via the computed covolume ratio (exact at any p) times the measured calibration
no safety verdict

heuristic_assumptions.statement: Transition shift is linear in log covolume per dimension
heuristic_assumptions.validation_plan: regress across p
